dish: Ainu cuisine — pocche-imo (fermented potato cakes), yuk (Ezo venison) set with foraged greens
n: Mingei Kissa Poronno, Akan Ainu Kotan (民芸喫茶 ポロンノ)
address: 4-7-8 Akanko Onsen, Akan-chō, Kushiro, Hokkaido, Japan (inside the Ainu Kotan)
w: Ainu cooking inside Hokkaido's largest Ainu village — pocche-imo and the yuk (venison) set, with gyōja-ninniku, fiddleheads and mushrooms gathered by the staff and deer from local hunters.

dish: sanshoku-don of Utoro-landed salmon and roe
n: Utoro Fishermen's Wives' Canteen (ウトロ漁協婦人部食堂)
address: 117 Utoro-higashi, Shari, Shari District, Hokkaido, Japan (by Utoro fishing port)
w: A 20-seat counter by the harbour run by local fishermen's wives — salmon landed at Utoro the same morning; queues out the door at lunch. Late April–late October.
